title: Typed event envelopes, partial-emits, and deterministic tool-handshake timeout acceptance
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Purpose: Clarify acceptance criteria for a new 'typed event envelope' format used by streaming structured outputs, define behavior for partial emissions (checkpointed fragments), and formalize deterministic timeout and retry semantics for tool/function handshakes.

Scope clarifications and recent scope change: originally scoped as a lightweight schema requirement; expanded to include: checkpoint IDs, sequence numbers for fragments, explicit repair/merge semantics for partial objects, deterministic handshake timeouts for synchronous tool calls, and observable telemetry hooks to measure repair rate and handshake latency. This ticket collects acceptance criteria, test cases, and rollout constraints so engineering and design can align on API surface and developer UX.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format: Every emitted structured object in streaming mode must be wrapped in a typed event envelope with these top-level fields (all names are case-sensitive): 'envelope_type' (string), 'schema_ref' (string), 'fragment_id' (string, opaque UUID), 'seq' (integer), 'is_final' (boolean), 'payload' (string or JSON string), 'checksum' (optional string). The schema_ref may be a static model-provided ID or a negotiated schema hash.

Partial emission reconciliation: Consumers must be able to reassemble fragments deterministically using (fragment_id, seq). If duplicate seq numbers are received for same fragment_id, the server must prefer the highest-seq 'is_final==true' fragment and provide reconciliation metadata in console logs.

Checkpointing: Streaming responses that emit large objects must emit periodic checkpoint events (envelope_type=='checkpoint') with a stable checkpoint_token (opaque string) that can be used to resume from the last successful commit point. Checkpoint events must include committed_seq (integer) and timestamp (RFC3339).

Tool handshake timeout: For synchronous tool/function calls initiated by the runtime, handshake must follow deterministic timeouts: initial handshake window = 3s, extended negotiation attempts = 2x backoff with maximum 9s total. If handshake does not complete within maximum window, runtime returns a standardized TOOL_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT error envelope to the client with a retriable flag set to true for transient failures.

Idempotency and replay: Tool invocations tied to a fragment must carry an idempotency token (string). If a client replays a partial fragment or re-invokes a tool using the same token, the tool gateway must detect replay and return a cached result where available or a 'REPLAY_DETECTED' marker in the envelope.

Streaming error modes: The system must distinguish between recoverable fragment errors (e.g., partial parse, backpressure) and terminal schema errors. Recoverable errors should emit envelope_type=='fragment_error' with 'repair_hint' field; terminal schema errors should emit 'fatal_schema_error' and close stream with clear error codes (policy documented in console).

Backpressure and flow control: Server must expose flow_control events to clients when the request queue or KV cache pressure exceeds thresholds (document thresholds in runtime-1.24). Clients receiving 'flow_control' must automatically attempt to resume at next checkpoint_token; server must not drop fragments silently.

Observability: Each handshake, fragment emission, checkpoint, and error event must generate telemetry with tags: env, model, customer_id (hashed), fragment_id, seq, handshake_latency_ms. Dashboards must show fragment_repair_rate and handshake_p50/p95/p99 for the release. Acceptance requires dashboard tiles and alert rules configured in the console-2026.03 dashboard.

Backward compatibility: If a client sends older envelope shapes (no checkpoint_token or seq), the runtime must accept but mark stream as 'compat_mode' in telemetry and apply best-effort reassembly. Acceptance requires a compatibility test matrix covering 3 older client SDK versions.

Legal/Security: If payloads contain PII flagged by runtime content classifiers, the server must redact sensitive fields in telemetry and add 'sensitive:true' to the envelope metadata. Acceptance requires KMS integration for any stored checkpoint tokens and documented retention policy.

Docs and SDKs: Public API docs and SDKs (Python/Node) must include examples for producing/consuming typed envelopes, resuming from checkpoint_token, and handling TOOL_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT. Acceptance requires code samples in the docs repo and a small sample app in examples/stream-repair demonstrating resume/repair flow.
test_cases: End-to-end: Start a streaming generation with a long object split into fragments, simulate an interrupted connection after fragment 7 of 12, reconnect with checkpoint_token and assert reassembly resumes at fragment 8 and final object checksum matches original.

Handshake timeout: Simulate tool gateway slowness to exceed 9s and assert client receives TOOL_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT error envelope with retriable flag true and that the runtime increments handshake_timeout metric.
Replay detection: Invoke the same tool call twice with identical idempotency tokens and assert the second request is detected as replay and returns cached result marker.

Backpressure signal: Generate 10x baseline traffic to trigger flow_control events; assert clients receive flow_control envelopes and that no fragments are dropped; verify alert on console if repair_rate > 5% for 5m.
Compatibility: Use legacy SDK that emits envelopes without seq/checkpoint and verify 'compat_mode' telemetry tag is generated and reassembly fallback succeeds on best-effort basis.
Security: Emit a fragment containing simulated PII and assert that telemetry redaction occurs and checkpoint tokens are written encrypted to KMS-backed store.
comments: 2026-03-06 10:12 - Asha Menon: Kickoff meeting notes attached; engineering requested deterministic timeout windows rather than configurable timeouts to reduce testing complexity.
2026-03-08 15:04 - Priya Shah (Eng): Raised concern about checkpoint token storage cost; proposed TTL of 24 hours, design added to ENG-1842.
2026-03-09 09:18 - Miguel Santos: Prototype handshake flow implemented in branch feat/handshake-timeouts (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123). Added initial telemetry tags per acceptance doc.

decision_log: Deterministic handshake windows chosen over full configurability to simplify client expectations and QA (decision date 2026-03-06).
Use of checkpoint_token TTL=24h to limit storage cost; will revisit for enterprise customers with longer retention needs (decision date 2026-03-08).
Emit explicit 'compat_mode' telemetry for older SDKs rather than breaking old clients (decision date 2026-03-09).
risks: Repair semantics can increase CPU cost on reassembly-heavy workloads; need to quantify in perf run.
Tight handshake windows may cause increased client-visible errors for high-latency regions; risk mitigated by retriable flag and auto-fallback to async tool invocation.
Checkpoint token sprawl if many ephemeral streams start but never complete; mitigated by TTL and background compaction job.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): runtime-1.24-canary in us-west1 for 48h with internal apps + 2 pilot customers.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 20% traffic over 7 days; monitor fragment_repair_rate and handshake_p95.
Phase 3: Full release after 2 weeks of steady metrics and resolved replay-detection edgecases; release notes and SDK updates published.
